artifactSchema.deliberateOmission: page-regions.json carries NO createdAt. It is a pure function of its inputs and the guarantee shipped is BYTE identity across two compiles; a timestamp would break that. The single clock reading lives in the run directory name and in report/region-summary.json.

regionIdScheme.scopeKey: "global", or the owning pageSourceId. NOT a route key: routes -> pageSourceId is many-to-one, so keying on a route would mint N identical regions for one shared page and force an arbitrary choice of "the" route. The brief's "scoped to its route key" is honoured in substance — every route that reaches the page is listed in region.pages[].routes and in the artifact's pages[] table — but the KEY itself is the pageSourceId. This is the one deliberate deviation from the brief's wording and it is called out here rather than buried.
regionIdScheme.landmarkKey: <landmark kind><document-order ordinal> — header1, nav1, nav2, main1, footer1 — or the literal "doc" for the implicit document scope that holds content outside every landmark. Assigned in a document-order pre-pass (src/regions/skeleton.ts:153 analyzeTree) so the candidate walk cannot influence numbering.
regionIdScheme.childPathDetail: slash-free chain of `tag:n` segments joined by `>`, measured from the LOCAL LANDMARK ROOT down to the region root, where n is the 1-based position among SAME-TAG element siblings (src/regions/skeleton.ts:104 pathSegment). `self` when the region root is the landmark root itself.
whyStable: TAG-SCOPED ordinal, not a dense child index — but read the limit honestly: it protects a region only from an insert of a DIFFERENT tag. A wrapper <div> inserted ahead of a <section> leaves `section:3` alone, where a dense index would have moved every following sibling; a <div> inserted ahead of a <div>-ROOTED region repaths it, because that is a same-tag insert. On real markup, whose region roots are overwhelmingly <div>s, this matters a lot: on the linear canary an upstream <div> insert at the top of <main> repaths 45 of 68 regions (66%), while the same <div> APPENDED repaths 0. Both directions are measured in scripts/smoke-regions.ts — §3 on the fixture (positive: both <section> ids survive an upstream <div> insert; negative control: the same-tag <div> sibling DOES shift; asymmetry: downstream loses no id, upstream does) and §7 on the real canary (0/68 downstream vs 45/68 upstream).
Measured from the LOCAL LANDMARK ROOT, not the document root, so a change in the outer shell above the landmark cannot repath everything below it.
Does NOT use the global nNNNNNN node ordinals — they renumber on any inserted node (src/interaction-explorer/types.ts).
Does NOT use persisted ancestorIds — they are truncated to 12 by src/recon-template/extract.ts, which drops exactly the TOP ancestors a region root lives among.
The structural skeleton hash is persisted BESIDE the id, never as it: the id must survive a markup edit inside the region, and the hash exists precisely to announce that edit.
regionIdScheme.uniqueness: Enforced. The compiler throws on a duplicate region id and on two roots in one tree resolving to the same address (src/regions/compile.ts). Verified on the real canaries: 68/68 unique on linear, 1014/1014 on stripe.

regionRootSelection.candidateSet: Closed and structural. Landmarks: header/nav/main/footer/aside plus role=banner|navigation|main|contentinfo|complementary. Sectioning: section/article/aside plus role=region. No AI, no semantic classification.
rules: 1. UNWRAP — collapse transparent single-element-child div/span wrappers (no role, no aria-label, no text of its own) so `div > div > <section>` yields ONE region, not three nested ones (src/regions/skeleton.ts:206).
2. SCOPE — a landmark opens a new id scope; its own path resets to `self` (src/regions/select-roots.ts:102).

3. SHELL — if a landmark or sectioning element sits within shellLookaheadDepth=6 levels below the node, the node is a CONTAINER of sections, so descend into its element children (src/regions/select-roots.ts:107). Bounded by descentDepthCap=12.
4. EMIT — otherwise the node is a region root, unless it holds no binding, no text and no media, in which case it is dropped as a spacer (src/regions/select-roots.ts:118).
regionRootSelection.htmlLandmarkScoping: <header>/<footer>/<aside> count as landmarks ONLY when not nested inside article/aside/main/nav/section — the HTML-AAM rule verbatim, not a tuning knob. This was added after measurement: the linear.app homepage carries nine <header> elements, eight of them card headers, and treating each as a landmark shattered the homepage into 59 regions with two depth-cap hits. With the rule: 25 regions, 0 depth-cap hits, whole-site 102 -> 68.
regionRootSelection.semanticMeaning: NOT attempted, as instructed. No region carries a hero/features/pricing label.

limitations: NO CONSUMER, BY INSTRUCTION. Nothing reads a PageRegion. No rendering, serving, release or QA path branches on one. The artifact is inert.
REGION SEMANTIC MEANING IS UNKNOWN and no attempt was made to infer it. A region is a seam, not a 'hero'.

GRANULARITY FOLLOWS THE MARKUP, and therefore varies a lot. linear.app: 25 regions on the homepage (which is section-rich) but 7 on /changelog, whose 3,234 bindings sit in a handful of large regions because the page's main content carries no sectioning markup. A page authored entirely in <div>s gets few, large regions. This is honest — there is no structural evidence there to cut on — but it means PageRegion granularity is NOT uniform and a consumer must not assume it is.

STRIPE CARRIES 449 REGIONS WHOSE LANDMARK IS A <header>. Those are body-scoped <header> elements nested in plain <div>s (not in sectioning content), so the HTML-AAM demotion rule does not reach them and each opens a landmark scope. It inflates stripe to ~56 regions/page. It is correct per the spec rule and it is not obviously wrong, but it is the largest single lever on stripe's region count and a future policy change there would move ids.

THE GLOBAL LIFT IS STRICT AND OFTEN MISSES A REAL SHARED SHELL. It requires identical landmarkKey, identical childPath, identical rootTag AND identical subtree hash on EVERY non-locale page. linear's footer is shared by 7 of 8 pages and stays page-scoped; stripe lifts only 2 regions. The cost is measured (nearGlobalGroups, nearGlobalMaxPages, globalCandidatesLandmarkQualifiedOnly) rather than assumed, and nothing was loosened on that evidence because loosening is a decision with a consumer.

THE UNWRAP RULE CAN ROOT A REGION AT A LEAF. `div > a` becomes a region rooted at the , `div > img` at the . No content is lost (the wrapper had no text of its own) but a consumer expecting every region root to be a block container would be surprised. Asserted explicitly in smoke §1 so the behavior is pinned, not accidental.

DESKTOP AND MOBILE ARE MERGED ON (landmarkKey, childPath) and split with an `@mobile` suffix only when the root TAG disagrees. Both canaries reported viewportRootMismatches=0, so that split path is exercised only by construction, never by real data. It was also the site of the one MAJOR defect found in verification: the GLOBAL branch never applied the suffix, so a landmark that swaps tag responsively on every page aborted the entire compile with `duplicate global region id`. Fixed and covered at both scopes (corrections C1, smoke §8) — but the honest statement remains that no real site has yet driven this path.

LANDMARK ORDINALS SHIFT if a landmark of the same kind is inserted before an existing one. That is rarer than a <div> insert and is the price of measuring paths from a local landmark root, but it is a real (and unavoidable, given the constraints) instability in the id.
THE PAGE-SCOPE KEY IS A pageSourceId, NOT A ROUTE KEY — a deliberate deviation from the brief's wording, taken because routes -> pageSourceId is many-to-one. Every route is still reported.

THE COMPILER READS A RECON-TEMPLATE RUN DIRECTORY, not a reconstruction run. It uses the runtime trees the template already carries in its app/reconstruction-data/, so it needs neither the reconstruction run nor the SiteSpec on disk. A template run whose app/ has been pruned cannot be region-compiled.

ORPHANS ARE ZERO ON BOTH CANARIES (0/9,929 and 0/24,518). That is a real measurement, not a disabled check: the two orphan/unresolved paths are proven live by planted bindings in smoke §6. But it means the orphan accounting has never been exercised by real data, and a site with slots on shell ancestors would be the first to test it.

THE ID SURVIVES A DOWNSTREAM INSERT AND OFTEN DOES NOT SURVIVE AN UPSTREAM ONE. Measured on the linear canary: a <div> inserted as the FIRST child of <main> on all 8 pages x 2 viewports repaths 45 of 68 regions (66%), e.g. p000001:rgn:main1:div:2>a:1 -> …div:3>a:1; the same <div> APPENDED repaths 0. The mechanism is that src/regions/skeleton.ts:104 pathSegment is a TAG-SCOPED ordinal, so on markup whose region roots are overwhelmingly <div>s a <div> insert IS a same-tag insert. The downstream-insert requirement is met; the upstream case is a real and unfixed cost of element-child paths, pinned in smoke §3 and §7 so it cannot drift out of view.
followUps: No consumer exists. Before anything is built on PageRegion, decide whether the global lift stays strict; counts.globalCandidatesLandmarkQualifiedOnly and counts.nearGlobalGroups are already persisted in every artifact to make that decision on measured evidence rather than on taste.

A Visual Editor selection layer can map a clicked element to its region with NO new DOM attribute: read data-wr-node off the element and look it up in the region occurrences. The artifact already carries every occurrence's nodeId per (page, viewport). Nothing else is needed.
structuralHash is a drift detector with no consumer yet. A recompile-and-diff check ('which regions changed markup since the last template compile?') is the cheapest useful thing to build on it.

Region granularity on <div>-only pages is the weakest part of the artifact. If a consumer needs uniform granularity, the honest fix is geometric (bounding boxes from the SiteSpec), not structural — and it would be a different, non-deterministic-by-construction input than this compiler takes.
src/regions/ is importable without src/recon-template/. Keep it that way: the (pageId, viewport, nodeId) join is the entire contract and it is what kept this Task out of the 25-importer file.

The global id assignment ranks variants open-endedly (@mobile, then @mobile2…) although at most two are structurally reachable. If a future change lets a page hold more than one draft per (address, root tag) — a third viewport, or a per-breakpoint capture — revisit that suffix vocabulary BEFORE it mints an id, because ids are the one thing here that cannot be renamed later.

No real site has yet produced viewportRootMismatches > 0. If one does, check the artifact for a `@mobile` id pair before assuming the global lift is complete: the two variants are separate regions and a consumer that expects one region per landmark path will see two.

corrections.title: Global lift never applied the @mobile suffix — a viewport root-tag mismatch on every page ABORTED the whole compile
corrections.reportedBy: independent verifier of the Wave-1 PageRegion compiler
corrections.defect: src/regions/compile.ts minted a global region id with regionIdOf("global", landmarkKey, childPath), which ignores rootTag, while the grouping key is `${landmarkKey}|${childPath}|${rootTag}|${structuralHash}` and DOES carry it. When a landmark renders as a different element tag at mobile than at desktop on every non-locale page, both tag variants satisfy the global-lift test, both lift, and both minted the identical id — hitting `if (emitted.has(regionId)) throw new RegionCompileError(...)`. The page-scoped branch already handled the same situation with a `@mobile` suffix; only the global branch was missing it.
corrections.impact: TOTAL compile failure, not a degraded result: `pnpm compile:regions` exits 1 with COMPILE ERROR and writes NO artifact at all, on a legitimate realistic input (a site that swaps a landmark's tag responsively).
corrections.reproductionBefore: Two pages with role="main" rendered as <main> at desktop and <article> at mobile -> THREW RegionCompileError: duplicate global region id global:rgn:main1:self. The SAME input with ONE page succeeded and produced p1:rgn:main1:self + p1:rgn:main1:self@mobile with viewportRootMismatches=1 — the suffix logic existed but was reachable only in page scope. Reproduced independently before the fix.
corrections.fix: src/regions/compile.ts:312-364 — a new `global id assignment` pass runs between the global lift and the emit loop. It buckets the lifted groups by their unsuffixed base id; a base id with ONE group keeps the unsuffixed id verbatim (the case every existing artifact was compiled under), and a base id with several ranks them so the variant built from the FEWEST `@mobile` drafts keeps the unsuffixed id, mirroring page scope, with the next taking `@mobile`. Ties — a site that renders the two tags the opposite way round on different pages — are broken by the root tag so the assignment is a function of the input, never of Map iteration order. The emit loop reads the assignment (src/regions/compile.ts:371) and keeps its duplicate-id throw as a backstop.
corrections.whyAtMostTwoVariants: Two drafts of ONE page share a (landmarkKey, childPath) address only when their root tags DIFFER, so a page contributes at most one draft per root tag; and a group that misses a page is not global. A base id can therefore hold at most two global groups. The rank is still written as an open-ended index (@mobile, then @mobile2…) so a third variant would be NAMED rather than silently collide.
corrections.behaviourAfter: 1 page -> p1:rgn:main1:self + p1:rgn:main1:self@mobile (unchanged). 2 or 3 pages -> global:rgn:main1:self + global:rgn:main1:self@mobile, both covering every page, viewportRootMismatches counted per page, no throw.

widerHazardReview.question: regionIdOf() ignores rootTag while the group key includes it — is there another reachable collision of the same shape?
widerHazardReview.answer: NO other reachable one was found, and the reasoning is structural rather than empirical. Page scope is protected by a stronger invariant than global scope had: the per-page drafts are a Map keyed on `${landmarkKey}|${childPath}` plus an `@mobile` discriminator, so ONE page holds at most one draft per (address, suffix) pair. Two page-scoped groups can therefore never both contribute an unsuffixed member from the same page, and their ids differ by the suffix. Global scope was the one place where the grouping crossed pages and so escaped that per-page Map — which is precisely the defect fixed. Global and page ids cannot collide with each other because the scopeKey namespaces them ('global' vs a pageSourceId), the only residual being a pageSourceId literally equal to the string 'global', which the template generator does not mint.
widerHazardReview.verifiedBy: Six adversarial fixtures compiled directly (all-split; genuine tie with opposite orientations on two pages; a 3-page mix where the <main> variant lifts globally while the <article> variant stays page-scoped on two pages; a split page beside an unsplit page of the OTHER tag, where the global id belongs to the tag the split page carries only at mobile; and three distinct root tags across three pages). Every case: ids unique, two compiles byte-identical, no throw. The genuine-tie and the page-scope-leftover cases are kept in the suite as §8; the rest were scratch.

corrections.title: The locality claim was materially overstated on real markup
corrections.defect: regionIdScheme.whyStable[0] said a wrapper <div> inserted ahead of a <section> leaves `section:3` alone. That is TRUE and it is proven in the suite, but as the HEADLINE stability claim it overstates the real-world protection, and the 11-entry limitations array named the landmark-ordinal instability without ever quantifying this much larger one.

measurement.what: An UPSTREAM <div> insert, unshifted as the first child of <main> on all 8 linear.app pages x 2 viewports (16 trees), versus the same <div> APPENDED as the last child.
measurement.upstream: 45 of 68 region ids lost (66%) — e.g. p000001:rgn:main1:div:2>a:1 -> p000001:rgn:main1:div:3>a:1. 6 new ids, 0 slotKey drift on the 23 survivors.
measurement.downstream: 0 of 68 ids lost, 6 new ids, 0 slotKey drift. Genuinely clean.
measurement.mechanism: src/regions/skeleton.ts:104 pathSegment is a TAG-SCOPED ordinal, so it protects a region only from an insert of a DIFFERENT tag. linear's region roots are overwhelmingly <div>s, so a <div> insert IS a same-tag insert for most of them.
